To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the heat content of an electrode metal droplet depends on the welding power supply type, the welding current, the arc voltage and the electrode diameter.
the heat content of molten electrode metal is determined by the voltage and current of the welding power source.
the type of power supply affects temperature, mass and surface area of electrode droplets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the method for calculating of the heat content of molten electrode metal in the process of manual arc welding.
the influence of the welding power source upon the heat content of electrode metal droplets in the process of welding with manual metal arc welding electrodes.

the development of a mathematical model for calculating the temperature, mass, and active surface area for the electrode metal droplets in relation to the energy parameters (voltage and current) of the power supplies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the type of welding power source affects the heat content of molten metal electrode droplets and thus the heat content of welding arc, and consequently it influences the welding quality.
the welding power supply with the constant voltage characteristic has the best properties for manual metal arc welds, which is confirmed by the results of the experimental investigations.
the heat content of electrode droplets depends upon the welding power supply type and its energy parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heat content of electrode droplets is the largest for the welding power supplies with the highest voltage and current values.
the heat content of a molten electrode metal is determined by its mass, active surface area and temperature.
it is necessary to consider the energy parameters of power supplies in the process of calculating heat content of the electrode metal droplets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heat content of electrode metal droplets is a function of the energy parameters of power supplies for manual arc welding.
the heat content of a droplet is determined by the type and voltage of the welding power source, the current intensity and the duration of the arc.
the heat content of molten electrode metal drops can be determined by the voltage drop across the arc, the welding current, and the arc length.
